fresh_translation: What happened, this is what will happen; and what has been done, this is what will be done; and there is nothing fresh under the sun.
brenton_translation: What is that which has been? the very thing which shall be: and what is that which has been done? the very thing which shall be done: and there is no new thing under the sun.

fresh_translation: Who will speak and say, "Look, this is new"? It already happened in the ages that came before us.
brenton_translation: Who is he that shall speak and say, Behold, this is new? it has already been in the ages that have passed before us.

fresh_translation: There is no memory for the first things, and even for the last things that come there will be no memory for them with the things yet to be at the end.
brenton_translation: There is no memorial to the first things; neither to the things that have been last shall their memorial be with them that shall be at the last time.

fresh_translation: I, Ecclesiastes, became king over Israel in Jerusalem.
brenton_translation: I the Preacher was king over Israel in Jerusalem.

fresh_translation: And I gave my heart to seek out and to inspect in wisdom concerning all things happening under heaven, because God gave evil distraction to the sons of man to be distracted in it.
brenton_translation: And I applied my heart to seek out and examine by wisdom concerning all things that are done under heaven, for God has given to the sons of men an evil trouble to be troubled therewith.

fresh_translation: I saw all works done under the sun, and look, all is vanity and choice of spirit.
brenton_translation: I beheld all the works that were wrought under the sun; and, behold, all were vanity and waywardness of spirit.

fresh_translation: What is twisted cannot be adorned, and what is lacking cannot be numbered.
brenton_translation: That which is crooked cannot be made straight: and deficiency cannot be numbered.

fresh_translation: I spoke in my heart saying, "I, look, grew great and added wisdom above all who were before me in Jerusalem," and my heart saw much wisdom and knowledge.
brenton_translation: I spoke in my heart, saying, Behold, I am increased, and have acquired wisdom beyond all who were before me in Jerusalem: also I applied my heart to know wisdom and knowledge.

fresh_translation: And I gave my heart to know wisdom and knowledge, parables and skill; I knew that this too is choice of spirit.
brenton_translation: And my heart knew much—wisdom, and knowledge, parables and understanding: I perceived that this also is waywardness of spirit.

fresh_translation: Because in much wisdom is much knowledge, and the one adding knowledge will add pain.
brenton_translation: For in the abundance of wisdom is abundance of knowledge; and he that increases knowledge will increase sorrow.

fresh_translation: I said in my heart, "Come now, I will test you in gladness and see in good," and look, this too is vanity.
brenton_translation: I said in my heart, Come now, I will prove thee with mirth, and behold thou good: and, behold, this is also vanity.

fresh_translation: To laughter I said, "Madness," and to gladness, "What does this do?"
brenton_translation: I said to laughter, Madness: and to mirth, Why doest thou this?

fresh_translation: I examined in my heart to draw my flesh into wine, and my heart led in wisdom, and to take hold upon folly until I should see what good there is for the sons of man, which they will do under the sun for the number of days of their life.
brenton_translation: And I examined whether my heart would excite my flesh as with wine, (though my heart guided me in wisdom,) and I desired to lay hold of mirth, until I should see of what kind is the good to the sons of men, which they should do under the sun all the days of their life.

fresh_translation: I magnified my work; I built houses for myself, I planted vineyards for myself.
brenton_translation: I enlarged my work; I built me houses; I planted me vineyards.

fresh_translation: I made gardens and parks for myself, and planted in them every fruit tree.
brenton_translation: I made me gardens and orchards, and planted in them every kind of fruit-tree.

fresh_translation: I made pools of waters for myself, to water from them a forest sprouting trees.
brenton_translation: I made me pools of water, to water from them the timber-bearing wood.

fresh_translation: I acquired male servants and female servants, and home-born servants became mine; and much possession of herds and flocks became mine beyond all who were before me in Jerusalem.
brenton_translation: I got servants and maidens, and servants were born to me in the house: also I had abundant possession of flocks and herds, beyond all who were before me in Jerusalem.

fresh_translation: I gathered for myself also silver and gold and treasures of kings and of the provinces; I made for myself singers and singing women and delights of the sons of man, a cupbearer and cupbearers.
brenton_translation: Moreover I collected for myself both silver and gold also, and the peculiar treasures of kings and provinces: I procured me singing men and singing women, and delights of the sons of men, a butler and female cupbearers.

fresh_translation: And I grew great and increased beyond all before me in Jerusalem, and my wisdom stood by me.
brenton_translation: So I became great, and advanced beyond all that were before me in Jerusalem: also my wisdom was established to me.

fresh_translation: And all that my eyes asked, I did not withhold from them; I did not restrain my heart from any gladness, because my heart rejoiced in all my toil, and this became my portion from all my toil.
brenton_translation: And whatever mine eyes desired, I withheld not from them, I withheld not my heart from all my mirth: for my heart rejoiced in all my labour; and this was my portion of all my labour.

fresh_translation: And I looked on all my works which my hands made and on toil in which I toiled to do, and look, all is vanity and choice of spirit, and there is no surplus under the sun.
brenton_translation: And I looked on all my works which my hands had wrought, and on my labour which I laboured to perform: and, behold, all was vanity and waywardness of spirit, and there is no advantage under the sun.

fresh_translation: And I looked to see wisdom and wandering and folly, because what kind of man will come after counsel? The things it made.
brenton_translation: Then I looked on to see wisdom, and madness, and folly: for who is the man who will follow after counsel, in all things wherein he employs it?

fresh_translation: And I saw that wisdom has surplus over folly as the surplus of light over darkness.
brenton_translation: And I saw that wisdom excels folly, as much as light excels darkness.

fresh_translation: The eyes of a wise man are in his head, but the fool walks in darkness; and I knew, yes I, that one meeting meets them all.
brenton_translation: The wise man's eyes are in his head; but the fool walks in darkness: and I perceived, even I, that one event shall happen to them all.

fresh_translation: And I said in my heart, "As the meeting of the fool, so also to me it will meet; and why then did I become wise more?" I spoke in my heart that this too is vanity, because a fool speaks from surplus.
brenton_translation: And I said in my heart, As the event of the fool is, so shall it be to me, even to me; and to what purpose have I gained wisdom? I said moreover in my heart, This is also vanity, because the fool speaks of his abundance.

fresh_translation: For there is no memory of the wise man with the fool forever, since already the days that are coming were all forgotten; and how will the wise man die with the fool?
brenton_translation: For there is no remembrance of the wise man with the fool for ever; forasmuch as now in the coming days all things are forgotten: and how shall the wise man die with the fool?

fresh_translation: And I hated life, because evil to me was work done under the sun, because all is vanity and choice of spirit.
brenton_translation: So I hated life; because the work that was wrought under the sun was evil before me: for all is vanity and waywardness of spirit.

fresh_translation: And I hated all my toil with which I toil under the sun, because I leave it to the man coming after me.
brenton_translation: And I hated the whole of my labour which I took under the sun; because I must leave it to the man who will come after me.

fresh_translation: And who knows whether he will be wise or a fool? Yet he rules over all my toil in which I toiled and became wise under the sun; and this too is vanity.
brenton_translation: And who knows whether he will be a wise man or a fool? and whether he will have power over all my labour in which I laboured, and wherein I grew wise under the sun? this is also vanity.

fresh_translation: And I turned to bid my heart farewell concerning all the toil in which I toiled under the sun.
brenton_translation: So I went about to dismiss from my heart all my labour wherein I had laboured under the sun.

fresh_translation: Because there is a man whose toil is in wisdom and knowledge and courage, and to a man who did not toil in it he will give his portion; and this too is vanity and a great evil.
brenton_translation: For there is such a man that his labour is in wisdom, and in knowledge, and in fortitude; yet this man shall give his portion to one who has not laboured therein. This is also vanity and great evil.

fresh_translation: For what comes to a man in all his toil and in the choice of his heart in which he toils under the sun?
brenton_translation: For it happens to a man in all his labour, and in the purpose of his heart wherein he labours under the sun.

fresh_translation: Because all his days are pains, and his distraction is wrath; even in the night his heart does not sleep, and this too is vanity.
brenton_translation: For all his days are days of sorrows, and vexation of spirit is his; in the night also his heart rests not. This is also vanity.

fresh_translation: There is no good in man except that he should eat and drink and show his soul good in his toil; and this too I saw, that it is from the hand of God.
brenton_translation: A man has nothing really good to eat, and to drink, and to shew his soul as good in his trouble. This also I saw, that it is from the hand of God.

fresh_translation: For who will eat and who will spare apart from him?
brenton_translation: For who shall eat, or who shall drink, without him?

fresh_translation: Because to the man who is good before him he gave wisdom and knowledge and gladness, but to the sinner he gave distraction, to add and to gather in order to give to one good before the face of God; because this too is vanity and choice of spirit.
brenton_translation: For God has given to the man who is good in his sight, wisdom, and knowledge, and joy: but he has given to the sinner trouble, to add and to heap up, that he may give to him that is good before God; for this is also vanity and waywardness of spirit.

fresh_translation: For all things there is a time, and a season for every matter under heaven.
brenton_translation: To all things there is a time, and a season for every matter under heaven.

fresh_translation: A time to bear and a time to die; a time to plant and a time to pull up what is planted.
brenton_translation: A time of birth, and a time to die; a time to plant, and a time to pluck up what has been planted;

fresh_translation: A time to kill and a time to heal; a time to tear down and a time to build.
brenton_translation: a time to kill, and a time to heal; a time to pull down, and a time to build up;

fresh_translation: A time to weep and a time to laugh; a time to mourn and a time to dance.
brenton_translation: a time to weep, and a time to laugh; a time to lament, and a time to dance;

fresh_translation: A time to throw stones and a time to gather stones; a time to embrace and a time to keep far from embracing.
brenton_translation: a time to throw stones, and a time to gather stones together; a time to embrace, and a time to abstain from embracing;

fresh_translation: A time to seek and a time to lose; a time to keep and a time to cast out.
brenton_translation: a time to seek, and a time to lose; a time to keep, and a time to cast away;

fresh_translation: A time to tear and a time to sew; a time to be silent and a time to speak.
brenton_translation: a time to rend, and a time to sew; a time to be silent, and a time to speak;

fresh_translation: A time to love and a time to hate; a time of war and a time of peace.
brenton_translation: a time to love, and a time to hate; a time of war, and a time of peace.

fresh_translation: What surplus is there to the doer in the things in which he toils?
brenton_translation: What advantage has he that works in those things wherein he labours?

fresh_translation: I saw the distraction which God gave to the sons of man to be distracted in it.
brenton_translation: I have seen all the trouble, which God has given to the sons of men to be troubled with.

fresh_translation: Together he made all things beautiful in its time, and also together he gave the age in their heart, so that man might not find the work that God made from the beginning even to the end.
brenton_translation: All the things which he has made are beautiful in his time: he has also set the whole world in their heart, that man might not find out the work which God has wrought from the beginning even to the end.

fresh_translation: I knew there is no good in them except to rejoice and to do good in his life.
brenton_translation: I know that there is no good in them, except for a man to rejoice, and to do good in his life.

fresh_translation: And also every man who eats and drinks and sees good in all his toil, it is a gift of God.
brenton_translation: Also in the case of every man who shall eat and drink, and see good in all his labour, this is a gift of God.

fresh_translation: I knew that all things whatever God made, these will be forever; on it there is nothing to add and from it nothing to take away, and God made it so that they may fear before his face.
brenton_translation: I know that whatsoever things God has done, they shall be for ever: it is impossible to add to it, and it is impossible to take away from it: and God has done it, that men may fear before him.

fresh_translation: What came to be already is, and what is to come to be already happened, and God will seek what is pursued.
brenton_translation: That which has been is now; and whatever things are appointed to be have already been; and God will seek out that which is past.

fresh_translation: And further, I saw under the sun: in the place of judgment, there was the impious one; and in the place of the righteous, there was the impious one.
brenton_translation: And moreover I saw under the sun the place of judgment, there was the ungodly one; and the place of righteousness, there was the godly one.

fresh_translation: I said in my heart, "The righteous and the ungodly God will judge, because there is a season for every matter and over every work."
brenton_translation: And I said in my heart, God will judge the righteous and the ungodly: for there is a time there for every action and for every work.

fresh_translation: There I said in my heart about the speech of the sons of man, that God will sort them out and show that they are beasts, even they themselves.
brenton_translation: I said in my heart, concerning the speech of the sons of man, God will judge them, and that to shew that they are beasts.

fresh_translation: Because the meeting of the sons of man and the meeting of the beast are one meeting for them; as the death of this one, so the death of that one, and one spirit is in all, and what did man have more than beast? Nothing, because all is vanity.
brenton_translation: Also to them is the event of the sons of man, and the event of the brute; one event befalls them: as is the death of the one, so also the death of the other; and there is one breath to all: and what has the man more than the brute? nothing; for all is vanity.

fresh_translation: All go to one place; all became from dust, and all return to dust.
brenton_translation: All go to one place; all were formed of the dust, and all will return to dust.

fresh_translation: And who knows whether the spirit of the sons of man goes upward, and the spirit of the beast goes down to earth?
brenton_translation: And who has seen the spirit of the sons of man, whether it goes upward? and the spirit of the beast, whether it goes downward to the earth?

fresh_translation: And I saw there is no good except that man will rejoice in his works, because this is his portion; for who will bring him to see what will happen after him?
brenton_translation: And I saw that there was no good, but that wherein a man shall rejoice in his works, for it is his portion, for who shall bring him to see any thing of that which shall be after him?

fresh_translation: And I turned and saw all the slanders happening under the sun, and look, the tears of those slandered, and there is no comforter for them, and from the hand of those slandering them is strength, and there is no comforter for them.
brenton_translation: So I returned, and saw all the oppressions that were done under the sun: and behold the tear of the oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of them that oppressed them was power; but they had no comforter:

fresh_translation: And I praised the dead, those already having died, above the living who are still alive until now.
brenton_translation: and I praised all the dead that had already died more than the living, as many as are alive until now.

fresh_translation: And better than both these is the one who has not yet come to be, who did not see the evil work done under the sun.
brenton_translation: Better also than both these is he who has not yet been, who has not seen all the evil work that is done under the sun.

fresh_translation: And I saw all the toil and all the manliness of the work, that it is jealousy of a man from his companion; and this too is vanity and choice of spirit.
brenton_translation: And I saw all labour, and all the diligent work, that this is a man's envy from his neighbour. This is also vanity and waywardness of spirit.

fresh_translation: A fool folded his hands and ate his own flesh.
brenton_translation: The fool folds his hands together, and eats his own flesh.

fresh_translation: Better one handful of rest than the filling of two hands with toil and choice of spirit.
brenton_translation: Better is a handful of rest than two handfuls of trouble and waywardness of spirit.

fresh_translation: And I turned and saw vanity under the sun:
brenton_translation: So I returned, and saw vanity under the sun.

fresh_translation: There is one and there is no second, and indeed there is no son or brother to him, and there is no end to all his toil; yet his eye is not filled with wealth. "And for whom do I toil and deprive my soul from goodness?" And this too is vanity and an evil distraction.
brenton_translation: There is one alone, and there is not a second; yea, he has neither son nor brother: yet there is no end to all his labour; neither is his eye satisfied with wealth; and for whom do I labour, and deprive my soul of good? this is also vanity, and an evil trouble.

fresh_translation: The two are good above the one, because they have a good reward in their toil.
brenton_translation: Two are better than one, seeing they have a good reward for their labour.

fresh_translation: Because if they fall, the one will raise his partner, and woe to the one when he falls and there is no second to raise him.
brenton_translation: For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow: but woe to him that is alone when he falls, and there is not a second to lift him up.

fresh_translation: And also if two lie down, there is warmth to them; but the one, how will he be warmed?
brenton_translation: Also if two should lie together, they also get heat: but how shall one be warmed alone?

fresh_translation: And if the one overpowers, the two will stand against him, and the threefold cord will not quickly be torn apart.
brenton_translation: And if one should prevail against him, the two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord shall not be quickly broken.

fresh_translation: Better a poor and wise child than an old and foolish king who no longer knew how to heed.
brenton_translation: Better is a poor and wise child than an old and foolish king, who knows not how to take heed any longer.

fresh_translation: Because from the house of the prisoners he will come out to reign, because indeed in his kingdom he was born poor.
brenton_translation: For he shall come forth out of the house of the prisoners to reign, because he also that was in his kingdom has become poor.

fresh_translation: I saw all the living who walk under the sun with the second young man who will stand in his place.
brenton_translation: I beheld all the living who were walking under the sun, with the second youth who shall stand up in each one's place.

fresh_translation: There is no end to all the people, to all who were before them; yet those last will not rejoice in him, because this too is vanity and choice of spirit.
brenton_translation: There is no end to all the people, to all who were before them: and the last shall not rejoice in him: for this also is vanity and waywardness of spirit.

fresh_translation: Guard your foot whenever you go into the house of God, and draw near to hear rather than to give the sacrifice of fools, for they are not knowing to do evil.
brenton_translation: Keep thy foot, whensoever thou goest to the house of God; and when thou art near to hear, let thy sacrifice be better than the gift of fools: for they know not that they are doing evil.

fresh_translation: Do not hurry with your mouth, and let not your heart hasten to bring out a word before the face of God, because God is in heaven and you are on earth; on this let your words be few.
brenton_translation: Be not hasty with thy mouth, and let not thine heart be swift to utter anything before God; for God is in heaven above, and thou upon earth: therefore let thy words be few.

fresh_translation: Because a dream comes in the multitude of distraction, and the voice of a fool in the multitude of words.
brenton_translation: For through the multitude of trial a dream comes; and a fool's voice is with a multitude of words.

fresh_translation: Just as if you vow a vow to God, do not delay to pay it, because there is no pleasure in fools; whatever you vow, pay.
brenton_translation: Whenever thou shalt vow a vow to God, defer not to pay it; for he has no pleasure in fools: pay thou therefore whatsoever thou shalt have vowed.

fresh_translation: Better that you not vow than that you vow and not pay.
brenton_translation: It is better that thou shouldest not vow, than that thou shouldest vow and not pay.

fresh_translation: Do not give your mouth to make your flesh sin, and do not say before the face of God that it was ignorance, lest God grow angry at your voice and ruin the works of your hands.
brenton_translation: Suffer not thy mouth to lead thy flesh to sin; and say not in the presence of God, It was an error: lest God be angry at thy voice, and destroy the works of thy hands.

fresh_translation: Because in the multitude of dreams and vanities and many words, instead fear God.
brenton_translation: For there is evil in a multitude of dreams and vanities and many words: but fear thou God.

fresh_translation: If you see slander of a poor man and robbery of judgment and righteousness in a province, do not marvel over the matter, because a high one watches over a high one, and high ones over them.
brenton_translation: If thou shouldest see the oppression of the poor, and the wresting of judgment and of justice in the land, wonder not at the matter: for there is a high one to watch over him that is high, and high ones over them.

fresh_translation: And land's surplus in everything is king over cultivated field.
brenton_translation: Also the abundance of the earth is for every one: the king is dependent on the tilled field.

fresh_translation: One loving silver will not be filled with silver, and who loved produce in their abundance? This too is vanity.
brenton_translation: He that loves silver shall not be satisfied with silver: and who has loved gain, in the abundance thereof? this is also vanity.

fresh_translation: In the multitude of good things, the eaters of it multiplied, and what advantage is there for its owner except seeing with his eyes?
brenton_translation: In the multitude of good they are increased that eat it: and what virtue has the owner, but the right of beholding it with his eyes?

fresh_translation: The sleep of a servant is sweet, whether little or much he eats; but the fullness of a rich man will not let him sleep.
brenton_translation: The sleep of a servant is sweet, whether he eat little or much: but to one who is satiated with wealth, there is none that suffers him to sleep.

fresh_translation: There is a sickness I saw under the sun: wealth kept by its owner for his harm.
brenton_translation: There is an infirmity which I have seen under the sun, namely, wealth kept for its owner to his hurt.

fresh_translation: And that wealth will perish in an evil distraction, and he begot a son and there is nothing in his hand.
brenton_translation: And that wealth shall perish in an evil trouble: and the man begets a son, and there is nothing in his hand.

fresh_translation: As he came out from his mother's womb, naked he will return to go as he came, and he will take nothing in his toil to go in his hand.
brenton_translation: As he came forth naked from his mother's womb, he shall return back as he came, and he shall receive nothing for his labour, that it should go with him in his hand.

fresh_translation: And this too is an evil sickness: just as he came, so he also will depart, and what surplus to him because he toils for wind?
brenton_translation: And this is also an evil infirmity: for as he came, so also shall he return: and what is his gain, for which he vainly labours?

fresh_translation: And indeed all his days in darkness and mourning and much wrath and sickness and bile.
brenton_translation: Yea, all his days are in darkness, and in mourning, and much sorrow, and infirmity, and wrath.

fresh_translation: Look, what I saw good, what is beautiful is to eat and to drink and to see goodness in all his toil with which he toils under the sun, the number of days of his life which God gave him, because this is his portion.
brenton_translation: Behold, I have seen good, that it is a fine thing for a man to eat and to drink, and to see good in all his labour in which he may labour under the sun, all the number of the days of his life which God has given to him: for it is his portion.

fresh_translation: And indeed every man to whom God gave wealth and possessions and empowered him to eat from it and to take his portion and rejoice in his toil, this is a gift of God.
brenton_translation: Yea, and as for every man to whom God has given wealth and possessions, and has given him power to eat thereof, and to receive his portion, and to rejoice in his labour; this is the gift of God.

fresh_translation: Because he will not remember many days of his life, because God distracts him in the gladness of his heart.
brenton_translation: For he shall not much remember the days of his life; for God troubles him in the mirth of his heart.

fresh_translation: There is an evil I saw under the sun, and it is much upon man.
brenton_translation: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is abundant with man:

fresh_translation: A man to whom God gives wealth and possessions and glory, so that his soul lacks nothing of all he desires, yet God does not empower him to eat from it, because a foreign man will eat it. This is vanity and grievous sickness.
brenton_translation: a man to whom God shall give wealth, and substance, and honour, and he wants nothing for his soul of all things that he shall desire, yet God shall not give him power to eat of it, for a stranger shall devour it: this is vanity, and an evil infirmity.

fresh_translation: If a man should beget a hundred and live many years, and however many days of his years may be, and his soul is not filled from good, and indeed burial did not happen for him, I said the stillborn is better than he.
brenton_translation: If a man beget a hundred children, and live many years, yea, however abundant the days of his years shall be, yet if his soul shall not be satisfied with good, and also he have no burial; I said, An untimely birth is better than he.

fresh_translation: Because in vanity it came and in darkness it goes, and in darkness its name will be covered.
brenton_translation: For he came in vanity, and departs in darkness, and his name shall be covered in darkness.

fresh_translation: And indeed it did not see the sun and did not know; rest is to this one more than to that one.
brenton_translation: Moreover he has not seen the sun, nor known rest: there is no more rest to this one than another.

fresh_translation: And if he lived a thousand years twice over and did not see good, do not all go to one place?
brenton_translation: Though he has lived to the return of a thousand years, yet he has seen no good: do not all go to one place?

fresh_translation: All the toil of man is for his mouth, yet the soul will not be filled.
brenton_translation: All the labour of a man is for his mouth, and yet the appetite shall not be satisfied.

fresh_translation: Because what surplus is there for the wise man over the fool? Because the poor man knows how to walk before life.
brenton_translation: For what advantage has the wise man over the fool, since even the poor knows how to walk in the direction of life?

fresh_translation: Better the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the soul; this too is vanity and choice of spirit.
brenton_translation: The sight of the eyes is better than that which wanders in soul: this is also vanity, and waywardness of spirit.

fresh_translation: Whatever came to be, its name already has been called, and it has been known what man is; and he will not be able to be judged with the one stronger than he.
brenton_translation: If anything has been, its name has already been called: and it is known what man is; neither can he contend with him who is stronger than he.

fresh_translation: Because there are many words multiplying vanity; what surplus is there to man?
brenton_translation: For there are many things which increase vanity.

fresh_translation: Because who knows what is good for man in life, the number of days of his vain life, and he made them in shadow? Because who will tell man what will be after him under the sun?
brenton_translation: What advantage has a man? for who knows what is good for a man in his life, during the number of the life of the days of his vanity? and he has spent them as a shadow; for who shall tell a man what shall be after him under the sun?

fresh_translation: A good name is above good oil, and the day of death above the day of his birth.
brenton_translation: A good name is better than good oil; and the day of death than the day of birth.

fresh_translation: Better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of drinking, because this is the end of every man, and the living one will give it to his heart.
brenton_translation: It is better to go to the house of mourning, than to go to the banquet house: since this is the end of every man; and the living man will apply good warning to his heart.

fresh_translation: Better anger than laughter, because by the gloom of a face the heart will be made good.
brenton_translation: Sorrow is better than laughter: for by the sadness of the countenance the heart will be made better.

fresh_translation: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning, and the heart of fools is in the house of gladness.
brenton_translation: The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth.

fresh_translation: Better to hear a rebuke of a wise man than a man hearing a song of fools.
brenton_translation: It is better to hear a reproof of a wise man, than for a man to hear the song of fools.

fresh_translation: Because as the sound of thorns under the cauldron, so is the laughter of fools, and this too is vanity.
brenton_translation: As the sound of thorns under a caldron, so is the laughter of fools: this is also vanity.

fresh_translation: Because slander drives a wise man mad and destroys the heart of his strength.
brenton_translation: For oppression makes a wise man mad, and destroys his noble heart.

fresh_translation: Better the end of a matter than its beginning; better a patient one than one high in spirit.
brenton_translation: The end of a matter is better than the beginning thereof: the patient is better than the high-minded.

fresh_translation: Do not hurry in your spirit to be angry, because anger will rest in the bosom of fools.
brenton_translation: Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry: for anger will rest in the bosom of fools.

fresh_translation: Do not say, "What happened that former days were better than these?" because you did not ask about this in wisdom.
brenton_translation: Say not, What has happened, that the former days were better than these? for thou dost not enquire in wisdom concerning this.

fresh_translation: Wisdom is good with inheritance, and a surplus to those seeing the sun.
brenton_translation: Wisdom is good with an inheritance: and there is an advantage by it to them that see the sun.

fresh_translation: Because in its shadow wisdom is as the shadow of silver, and the surplus of the knowledge of wisdom will give life to its possessor.
brenton_translation: For wisdom in its shadow is as the shadow of silver: and the excellence of the knowledge of wisdom will give life to him that has it.

fresh_translation: See the works of God, because who can set in order what God twists?
brenton_translation: Behold the works of God: for who shall be able to straighten him whom God has made crooked?

fresh_translation: In the day of goodness, live in good, and in the day of evil, see: indeed God made this corresponding to that, so that the man should find nothing after him.
brenton_translation: In the day of prosperity live joyfully, and consider in the day of adversity: consider, I say, God also has caused the one to agree with the other for this reason, that man should find nothing after him.

fresh_translation: I saw all things in the days of my vanity: there is a righteous man perishing in his righteousness, and there is an impious man remaining in his evil.
brenton_translation: I have seen all things in the days of my vanity: there is a just man perishing in his justice, and there is an ungodly man remaining in his wickedness.

fresh_translation: Do not become very righteous, and do not make yourself excessively wise, lest perhaps you be stunned.
brenton_translation: Be not very just; neither be very wise: lest thou be confounded.

fresh_translation: Do not be very ungodly, and do not become hard, lest you die not in your time.
brenton_translation: Be not very wicked; and be not stubborn: lest thou shouldest die before thy time.

fresh_translation: It is good that you take hold in this, and from that do not let your hand rest, because the one fearing God will come out with all these.
brenton_translation: It is well for thee to hold fast by this; also by this defile not thine hand: for to them that fear God all things shall come forth well.

fresh_translation: Wisdom will help the wise man above ten rulers who are in the city.
brenton_translation: Wisdom will help the wise man more than ten mighty men which are in the city.

fresh_translation: Because there is not a righteous man on earth who will do good and not sin.
brenton_translation: For there is not a righteous man in the earth, who will do good, and not sin.

fresh_translation: And indeed to all the words they may speak, do not set your heart, so that you may not hear your servant cursing you.
brenton_translation: Also take no heed to all the words which ungodly men shall speak; lest thou hear thy servant cursing thee.

fresh_translation: Because many times your heart will work evil against you, and in many ways it will hurt, because you too cursed others.
brenton_translation: For many times he shall trespass against thee, and repeatedly shall he afflict thine heart; for thus also hast thou cursed others.

fresh_translation: All these I tested in wisdom; I said, "I will become wise,"
brenton_translation: All these things have I proved in wisdom: I said, I will be wise; but it was far from me.

fresh_translation: and it was far from me, far beyond what it was, and deep, deep; who will find it?
brenton_translation: That which is far beyond what was, and a great depth, who shall find it out?

fresh_translation: I circled, I and my heart, to know and to inspect and to seek wisdom and reckoning, and to know the folly of an ungodly one and hardness and madness.
brenton_translation: I and my heart went round about to know, and to examine, and to seek wisdom, and the account of things, and to know the folly and trouble and madness of the ungodly man.

fresh_translation: And I find more bitter than death the woman whose heart is hunting nets and seines, and her hands are bonds; the good one before the face of God will be rescued from her, and the sinner will be caught in her.
brenton_translation: And I find her to be, and I will pronounce to be more bitter than death the woman which is a snare, and her heart nets, who has a band in her hands: he that is good in the sight of God shall be delivered from her; but the sinner shall be caught by her.

fresh_translation: Look, this I found, said the Ecclesiastes, one by one to find a reckoning.
brenton_translation: Behold, this have I found, said the Preacher, seeking by one at a time to find out the account,

fresh_translation: Which my soul still sought and I did not find: one man among a thousand I found, but a woman among all these I did not find.
brenton_translation: which my soul sought after, but I found not: for I have found one man of a thousand; but a woman in all these I have not found.

fresh_translation: Except look, this I found: what God made with man is upright, but they sought many reckonings.
brenton_translation: But, behold, this have I found, that God made man upright; but they have sought out many devices.

fresh_translation: Who knows a wise man, and who knows the explanation of a word? The wisdom of a man gives light to his face, and the hardness of his face will be hated.
brenton_translation: A man's wisdom will lighten his countenance; but a man of shameless countenance will be hated.

fresh_translation: Keep the king's mouth, and because of the word of God's oath do not hurry.
brenton_translation: Observe the commandment of the king, and that because of the word of the oath of God.

fresh_translation: Go from his face; do not stand in an evil matter, because whatever he wishes he will do.
brenton_translation: Be not hasty; thou shalt go forth out of his presence: stand not in an evil matter; for he will do whatsoever he shall please,

fresh_translation: As a king speaks exercising authority, and who will say to him, "What are you doing?"
brenton_translation: even as a king having power: and who will say to him, What doest thou?

fresh_translation: The one keeping a command will know no evil thing, and the heart of a wise man knows a time of judgment.
brenton_translation: He that keeps the commandment shall not know an evil thing: and the heart of the wise knows the time of judgment.

fresh_translation: Because for every matter there is a time and judgment, because the knowledge of man is much upon him.
brenton_translation: For to every thing there is time and judgment; for the knowledge of a man is great to him.

fresh_translation: Because there is no one knowing what will be, because as it will be, who will tell him?
brenton_translation: For there is no one that knows what is going to be: for who shall tell him how it shall be?

fresh_translation: There is no man exercising authority over the spirit to restrain the spirit, and there is no authority in the day of death, and there is no discharge in war, and ungodliness will not rescue its possessor.
brenton_translation: There is no man that has power over the spirit to retain the spirit; and there is no power in the day of death: and there is no discharge in the day of battle; neither shall ungodliness save her votary.

fresh_translation: And with all this I saw and gave my heart to every work done under the sun, all in which man exercised authority over man to harm him.
brenton_translation: So I saw all this, and I applied my heart to every work that has been done under the sun; all the things wherein man has power over man to afflict him.

fresh_translation: And then I saw ungodly men brought into tombs, and they went from the holy place and were praised in the city because thus they did; this too is vanity.
brenton_translation: And then I saw the ungodly carried into the tombs, and that out of the holy place: and they departed, and were praised in the city, because they had done thus: this also is vanity.

fresh_translation: Because rebuttal against those doing evil does not happen quickly; because of this the heart of the sons of man was fully assured in them to do evil.
brenton_translation: Because there is no contradiction made on the part of those who do evil quickly, therefore the heart of the children of men is fully determined in them to do evil.

fresh_translation: The one who sinned did evil from then and from length to him; yet I know that good will be for those fearing God, so that they may fear before his face.
brenton_translation: He that has sinned has done evil from that time, and long from beforehand: nevertheless I know, that it is well with them that fear God, that they may fear before him:

fresh_translation: And good will not be for the ungodly man, and he will not lengthen days in shadow, because he does not fear before the face of God.
brenton_translation: but it shall not be well with the ungodly, and he shall not prolong his days, which are as a shadow; forasmuch as he fears not before God.

fresh_translation: There is vanity done upon the earth: there are righteous ones to whom it reaches as the work of ungodly ones, and there are ungodly ones to whom it reaches as the work of righteous ones; I said that this too is vanity.
brenton_translation: There is a vanity which is done upon the earth; that there are righteous persons to whom it happens according to the doing of the ungodly; and there are ungodly men, to whom it happens according to the doing of the just: I said, This is also vanity.

fresh_translation: And I praised the gladness, because there is no good for a man under the sun except to eat and to drink and to rejoice, and this will stay with him in his toil all the days of his life which God gave him under the sun.
brenton_translation: Then I praised mirth, because there is no good for a man under the sun, but to eat, and drink, and be merry: and this shall attend him in his labour all the days of his life, which God has given him under the sun.

fresh_translation: In which I gave my heart to know wisdom and to see the distraction done upon the earth, because even by day and by night there is no sleep in his eyes, seeing.
brenton_translation: Whereupon I set my heart to know wisdom, and to perceive the trouble that was wrought upon the earth: for there is that neither by day nor night sees sleep with his eyes.

fresh_translation: And I saw all the works of God, that man will not be able to find out the work done under the sun. However much a man toils to seek, he will not find; and however much a wise man says to know, he will not be able to find.
brenton_translation: And I beheld all the works of God, that a man shall not be able to discover the work which is wrought under the sun; whatsoever things a man shall endeavour to seek, however a man may labour to seek it, yet he shall not find it; yea, how much soever a wise man may speak of knowing it, he shall not be able to find it: for I applied all this to my heart, and my heart has seen all this.

fresh_translation: Because with all this I gave into my heart, and my heart saw all this: the righteous and the wise and their works are in the hand of God; yet love and hatred a man does not know; all things are before them.
brenton_translation: I saw that the righteous, and the wise, and their works, are in the hand of God: yea, there is no man that knows either love or hatred, though all are before their face.

fresh_translation: Vanity is in all things: one meeting is for the righteous and the ungodly, for the good and the evil, for the clean and the unclean, for the one sacrificing and the one not sacrificing; as the good one, so the sinner; as the one swearing, so the one fearing an oath.
brenton_translation: Vanity is in all: there is one event to the righteous, and to the wicked; to the good, and to the bad; both to the pure, and to the impure; both to him that sacrifices, and to him that sacrifices not: as is the good, so is the sinner: as is the swearer, even so is he that fears an oath.

fresh_translation: This is evil in all done under the sun: one meeting is in all, and indeed the heart of the sons of man was filled with evil, and madness is in their heart during their life, and after them is to the dead.
brenton_translation: There is this evil in all that is done under the sun, that there is one event to all: yea, the heart of the sons of men is filled with evil, and madness is in their heart during their life, and after that they go to the dead.

fresh_translation: Because for whoever joins with all the living there is hope, because a living dog is better than a dead lion.
brenton_translation: For who is he that has fellowship with all the living? there is hope of him: for a living dog is better than a dead lion.

fresh_translation: Because the living will know that they will die, but the dead know nothing, and there is no wage for them anymore, because the memory of them was forgotten.
brenton_translation: For the living will know that they shall die: but the dead know nothing, and there is no longer any reward to them; for their memory is lost.

fresh_translation: And indeed their love and indeed their hatred and indeed their zeal already perished, and there is no portion for them anymore forever in anything done under the sun.
brenton_translation: Also their love, and their hatred, and their envy, have now perished; yea, there is no portion for them any more for ever in all that is done under the sun.

fresh_translation: Come, eat your bread in gladness and drink your wine in a good heart, because God already took pleasure in your works.
brenton_translation: Go, eat thy bread with mirth, and drink thy wine with a joyful heart; for now God has favourably accepted thy works.

fresh_translation: At every time let your garments be white, and let oil on your head not fail.
brenton_translation: Let thy garments be always white; and let not oil be wanting on thine head.

fresh_translation: See life with a woman whom you loved all the days of your life of vanity, those given to you under the sun, all the days of your vanity, because this is your portion in your life and in your toil with which you toil under the sun.
brenton_translation: And see life with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which are given thee under the sun: for that is thy portion in thy life, and in thy labour wherein thou labourest under the sun.

fresh_translation: All that your hand finds to do, do by your strength, because there is no work and reckoning and knowledge and wisdom in Hades where you go there.
brenton_translation: Whatsoever thine hand shall find to do, do with all thy might; for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in Hades whither thou goest.

fresh_translation: I turned and saw under the sun that the race is not to the swift, nor is war to the strong, and indeed neither is bread to the wise, and indeed neither is wealth to those with understanding, and indeed neither is favor to those knowing, because time and encounter will meet them all.
brenton_translation: I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, nor yet bread to the wise, nor yet wealth to men of understanding, nor yet favour to men of knowledge; for time and chance will happen to them all.

fresh_translation: Because indeed a man did not know his time: as fish caught in an evil net and as birds caught in a snare, as they are trapped, so the sons of man are trapped for an evil time when it falls upon them suddenly.
brenton_translation: For surely man also knows not his time: as fishes that are taken in an evil net, and as birds that are caught in a snare; even thus the sons of men are snared at an evil time, when it falls suddenly upon them.

fresh_translation: And this too I saw as wisdom under the sun, and it is great to me.
brenton_translation: This I also saw to be wisdom under the sun, and it is great before me:

fresh_translation: A small city, and few men in it, and a great king came against it and surrounded it and built great siegeworks against it.
brenton_translation: suppose there were a little city, and few men in it; and there should come against it a great king, and surround it, and build great mounds against it;

fresh_translation: And he found in it a poor wise man, and he will save the city by his wisdom, and man did not remember that poor man.
brenton_translation: and should find in it a poor wise man, and he should save the city through his wisdom: yet no man would remember that poor man.

fresh_translation: And I said wisdom is good above strength, yet the wisdom of the poor man is despised and his words are not heard.
brenton_translation: And I said, Wisdom is better than power: yet the wisdom of the poor man is set at nought, and his words not listened to.

fresh_translation: The words of the wise in quiet are heard above the cry of rulers among follies.
brenton_translation: The words of the wise are heard in quiet more than the cry of them that rule in folly.

fresh_translation: Wisdom is good above weapons of war, and one sinner will destroy much good.
brenton_translation: Wisdom is better than weapons of war: and one sinner will destroy much good.

fresh_translation: Deadly flies rot a compound of perfumed oil; a little wisdom is held precious above great glory of folly.
brenton_translation: Pestilent flies will corrupt a preparation of sweet ointment: and a little wisdom is more precious than great glory of folly.

fresh_translation: The heart of the wise is at his right, and the heart of a fool is at his left.
brenton_translation: A wise man's heart is at his right hand; but a fool's heart at his left.

fresh_translation: And indeed on the road whenever a fool walks, his heart will lack, and what he thinks is all folly.
brenton_translation: Yea, and whenever a fool walks by the way, his heart will fail him, and all that he thinks of is folly.

fresh_translation: If the spirit of the ruler rises upon you, do not leave your place, because healing will put great sins to rest.
brenton_translation: If the spirit of the ruler rise up against thee, leave not thy place; for soothing will put an end to great offences.

fresh_translation: There is evil I saw under the sun, like an involuntary thing that went out from the face of the ruler.
brenton_translation: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, wherein an error has proceeded from the ruler.

fresh_translation: The fool was given in great heights, and rich men will sit in a low place.
brenton_translation: The fool has been set in very high places, while rich men would sit in a low one.

fresh_translation: I saw slaves on horses and rulers walking like slaves upon the earth.
brenton_translation: I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking as servants on the earth.

fresh_translation: The one digging a pit will fall into it, and a snake will bite the one pulling down a wall.
brenton_translation: He that digs a pit shall fall into it; and him that breaks down a hedge a serpent shall bite.

fresh_translation: The one removing stones will be hurt by them; the one splitting wood will be endangered by them.
brenton_translation: He that removes stones shall be troubled thereby; he that cleaves wood shall be endangered thereby.

fresh_translation: If the iron grows dull and he has disturbed its face, then he will strengthen force; and the surplus for skill is wisdom.
brenton_translation: If the axe-head should fall off, then the man troubles his countenance, and he must put forth more strength: and in that case skill is of no advantage to a man.

fresh_translation: If the snake bites without whispering, there is no surplus for the charmer.
brenton_translation: If a serpent bite when there is no charmer's whisper, then there is no advantage to the charmer.

fresh_translation: The words of the mouth of the wise are favor, and the lips of a fool will swallow him.
brenton_translation: The words of a wise mouth are gracious: but the lips of a fool will swallow him up.

fresh_translation: The beginning of the words of his mouth is folly, and the last of his mouth is evil madness.
brenton_translation: The beginning of the words of his mouth is folly: and the end of his talk mischievous madness.

fresh_translation: And the fool multiplies words; a man does not know what has happened, and what will be after him, who will tell him?
brenton_translation: A fool moreover multiplies words: man knows not what has been, nor what will be: who shall tell him what will come after him?

fresh_translation: The toil of fools will weary them, because one did not know how to go into a city.
brenton_translation: The labour of fools will afflict them, as that of one who knows not to go to the city.

fresh_translation: Woe to you, city, whose king is young, and your rulers eat in the morning.
brenton_translation: Woe to thee, O city, whose king is young, and thy princes eat in the morning!

fresh_translation: Blessed are you, land whose king is a son of nobles, and your rulers will eat at the right time in strength and will not be ashamed.
brenton_translation: Blessed art thou, O land, whose king is a son of nobles, and whose princes shall eat seasonably, for strength, and shall not be ashamed.

fresh_translation: In sloth the roof-beam will be brought low, and in idleness of hands the house will drip.
brenton_translation: By slothful neglect a building will be brought low: and by idleness of the hands the house will fall to pieces.

fresh_translation: For laughter they make bread, and wine gladdens the living ones, and silver answers all things.
brenton_translation: Men prepare bread for laughter, and wine and oil that the living should rejoice: but to money all things will humbly yield obedience.

fresh_translation: Even in your conscience do not curse a king, and in the chambers of your bedchambers do not curse a rich man, because a bird of heaven will carry the voice, and the winged one will report a word.
brenton_translation: Even in thy conscience, curse not the king; and curse not the rich in thy bedchamber: for a bird of the air shall carry thy voice, and that which has wings shall report thy speech.

fresh_translation: Send your bread upon the face of the water, because in the multitude of days you will find it.
brenton_translation: Send forth thy bread upon the face of the water: for thou shalt find it after many days.

fresh_translation: Give a portion to seven and indeed to eight, because you do not know what evil will be upon the earth.
brenton_translation: Give a portion to seven, and also to eight; for thou knowest not what evil there shall be upon the earth.

fresh_translation: If the clouds are filled with rain, they pour upon the earth; and if a tree falls in the south, and if in the north, in the place where the tree falls, there it will be.
brenton_translation: If the clouds be filled with rain, they pour it out upon the earth: and if a tree fall southward, or if it fall northward, in the place where the tree shall fall, there it shall be.

fresh_translation: The one watching the wind will not sow, and the one looking in the clouds will not reap.
brenton_translation: He that observes the wind sows not; and he that looks at the clouds will not reap.

fresh_translation: As you do not know what the way of spirit is, as bones are in the womb of a pregnant woman, so you will not know the works of God, who will make all things.
brenton_translation: Among whom none knows what is the way of the wind: as the bones are hid in the womb of a pregnant woman, so thou shalt not know the works of God, even all things whatsoever he shall do.

fresh_translation: In the morning sow your seed, and till evening do not let your hand rest, because you do not know which will prosper, this or that, and if both together are good.
brenton_translation: In the morning sow thy seed, and in the evening let not thine hand be slack: for thou knowest not what sort shall prosper, whether this or that, or whether both shall be good alike.

fresh_translation: And the light is sweet, and it is good for the eyes to see with the sun.
brenton_translation: Moreover the light is sweet, and it is good for the eyes to see the sun.

fresh_translation: Because even if a man lives many years, in all of them he will rejoice, and he will remember the days of darkness, because they will be many; all that is coming is vanity.
brenton_translation: For even if a man should live many years, and rejoice in them all; yet let him remember the days of darkness; for they shall be many. All that comes is vanity.

fresh_translation: Rejoice, young man, in your youth, and let your heart do you good in the days of your youth, and walk in the ways of your heart and in the sight of your eyes, and know that for all these God will bring you in judgment.
brenton_translation: Rejoice, O young man, in thy youth; and let thy heart cheer thee in the days of thy youth, and walk in the ways of thy heart blameless, but not in the sight of thine eyes: yet know that for all these things God will bring thee into judgment.

fresh_translation: And remove anger from your heart and put evil from your flesh, because youth and folly are vanity.
brenton_translation: Therefore remove sorrow from thy heart, and put away evil from thy flesh: for youth and folly are vanity.

fresh_translation: And remember the one who created you in the days of your youth, until the days of evil do not come and years arrive in which you will say, "There is no delight for me in them."
brenton_translation: And remember thy Creator in the days of thy youth, before the days of evil come, and the years overtake thee in which thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them.

fresh_translation: Until the sun and the light and the moon and the stars are not darkened and the clouds return after the rain.
brenton_translation: While the sun and light are not darkened, nor the moon and the stars; nor the clouds return after the rain:

fresh_translation: In the day whenever the guards of the house will be shaken and the men of strength twisted and the grinders cease because they became few and those seeing through the openings grow dark,
brenton_translation: in the day wherein the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the mighty men shall become bent, and the grinding women cease because they have become few, and the women looking out at the windows be dark;

fresh_translation: and doors in the market will be shut in the weakness of the sound of the grinder, and he will rise at the sound of the sparrow, and all daughters of song will be brought low.
brenton_translation: and they shall shut the doors in the market-place, because of the weakness of the voice of her that grinds at the mill; and he shall rise up at the voice of the sparrow, and all the daughters of song shall be brought low;

fresh_translation: And indeed they will look from a height and terrors will be in the road, and the almond will blossom and the locust will grow fat and the caperberry will be scattered, because a man went to the house of his age, and mourners circled in the market.
brenton_translation: and they shall look up, and fears shall be in the way, and the almond tree shall blossom, and the locust shall increase, and the caper shall be scattered: because man has gone to his eternal home, and the mourners have gone about the market:

fresh_translation: Until the silver cord is not overturned and the flower of gold crushed and a water jar broken at the spring and the wheel crushed upon the pit.
brenton_translation: before the silver cord be let go, or the choice gold be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel run down to the cistern;

fresh_translation: And the dust returns upon the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God who gave it.
brenton_translation: before the dust also return to the earth as it was, and the spirit return to God who gave it.

fresh_translation: Vanity of vanities, said the Ecclesiastes; all is vanity.
brenton_translation: Vanity of vanities, said the Preacher; all is vanity.

fresh_translation: And beyond that, because the Ecclesiastes became wise, he still taught knowledge with the people, and his ear traced out ordered parables.
brenton_translation: And because the Preacher was wise above others, so it was that he taught man excellent knowledge, and the ear will trace out the parables.

fresh_translation: The Ecclesiastes sought much to find words of delight, and written uprightness, the words of truth.
brenton_translation: The Preacher sought diligently to find out acceptable words, and a correct writing, even words of truth.

fresh_translation: The words of the wise are as goads, and as nails planted, those from gatherings were given from one shepherd.
brenton_translation: The words of the wise are as goads, and as nails firmly fastened, which have been given from one shepherd by agreement.

fresh_translation: My son, beware of making many books; there is no end, and much study is weariness of flesh.
brenton_translation: And moreover, my son, guard thyself by means of them: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh.

fresh_translation: The end of the matter, all is heard: fear God and keep his commandments, because this is the whole man.
brenton_translation: Hear the end of the matter, the sum: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole man.

fresh_translation: Because with every work God will bring into judgment, with every overlooked thing, whether good or whether evil.
brenton_translation: For God will bring every work into judgment, with everything that has been overlooked, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.

fresh_translation: The Song of Songs, which is Solomon's.
brenton_translation: The Song of songs, which is Solomon's.

fresh_translation: Let him kiss me with kisses of his mouth, because your breasts are better than wine.
brenton_translation: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth: for thy breasts are better than wine.

fresh_translation: And the scent of your perfumes is above all spices; your name is poured-out perfume, therefore young women loved you.
brenton_translation: And the smell of thine ointments is better than all spices: thy name is ointment poured forth; therefore do the young maidens love thee.

fresh_translation: They drew you; after you, into the scent of your perfumes we will run. The king brought me into his chamber. We will rejoice and be glad in you; we will love your breasts more than wine; the upright loved you.
brenton_translation: They have drawn thee: we will run after thee, for the smell of thine ointments: the king has brought me into his closet: let us rejoice and be glad in thee; we will love thy breasts more than wine: righteousness loves thee.

fresh_translation: Black I am and beautiful, daughters of Jerusalem, like tents of Kedar, like skins of Solomon.
brenton_translation: I am black, but beautiful, ye daughters of Jerusalem, as the tents of Kedar, as the curtains of Solomon.

fresh_translation: Do not look at me because I am darkened, because the sun looked past me. The sons of my mother fought in me; they set me keeping vineyards; my own vineyard I did not keep.
brenton_translation: Look not upon me, because I am dark, because the sun has looked unfavourably upon me: my mother's sons strove with me; they made me keeper in the vineyards; I have not kept my own vineyard.

fresh_translation: Tell me, you whom my soul loved, where do you shepherd, where do you rest at noon, lest I become as one veiled over flocks of your companions?
brenton_translation: Tell me, thou whom my soul loves, where thou tendest thy flock, where thou causest them to rest at noon, lest I become as one that is veiled by the flocks of thy companions.

fresh_translation: If you do not know yourself, beautiful among women, go out on the heels of the flocks and shepherd your young goats by the tents of the shepherds.
brenton_translation: If thou know not thyself, thou fair one among women, go thou forth by the footsteps of the flocks, and feed thy kids by the shepherds' tents.

fresh_translation: To my mare among the chariots of Pharaoh I likened you, my dear one.
brenton_translation: I have likened thee, my companion, to my horses in the chariots of Pharao.

fresh_translation: How beautiful are your cheeks as turtledoves, your neck as necklaces.
brenton_translation: How are thy cheeks beautiful as those of a dove, thy neck as chains!

fresh_translation: We will make for you likenesses of gold with marks of silver.
brenton_translation: We will make thee figures of gold with studs of silver.

fresh_translation: Until the king is at his recline, my nard gave its scent.
brenton_translation: So long as the king was at table, my spikenard gave forth its smell.

fresh_translation: A bundle of myrrh is my beloved to me; between my breasts he will lodge.
brenton_translation: My kinsman is to me a bundle of myrrh; he shall lie between my breasts.

fresh_translation: A cluster of cypress is my beloved to me in the vineyards of En-gedi.
brenton_translation: My kinsman is to me a cluster of camphor in the vineyards of Engaddi.

fresh_translation: Look, you are beautiful, my dear one, look, you are beautiful; your eyes are doves.
brenton_translation: Behold, thou art fair, my companion; behold, thou art fair; thine eyes are doves.

fresh_translation: Look, you are beautiful, my beloved, and indeed lovely; our bed is shadowed.
brenton_translation: Behold, thou art fair, my kinsman, yea, beautiful, overshadowing our bed.

fresh_translation: The beams of our houses are cedars, our rafters are cypresses.
brenton_translation: The beams of our house are cedars, our ceilings are of cypress.

fresh_translation: I am a flower of the field, a lily of the valleys.
brenton_translation: I am a flower of the plain, a lily of the valleys.

fresh_translation: As a lily in the midst of thorns, so my dear one in the midst of the daughters.
brenton_translation: As a lily among thorns, so is my companion among the daughters.

fresh_translation: As an apple tree among the trees of the grove, so my beloved in the midst of the sons. In his shadow I desired and sat, and his fruit was sweet to my palate.
brenton_translation: As the apple among the trees of the wood, so is my kinsman among the sons. I desired his shadow, and sat down, and his fruit was sweet in my throat.

fresh_translation: Bring me into the house of wine; arrange love upon me.
brenton_translation: Bring me into the wine house; set love before me.

fresh_translation: Strengthen me with perfumes, heap me with apples, because I am wounded by love.
brenton_translation: Strengthen me with perfumes, stay me with apples: for I am wounded with love.

fresh_translation: His left is under my head, and his right will embrace me.
brenton_translation: His left hand shall be under my head, and his right hand shall embrace me.

fresh_translation: I bound you by oath, daughters of Jerusalem, by the powers and by the strengths of the field, that you not rouse and awaken love until it wishes.
brenton_translation: I have charged you, ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the powers and by the virtues of the field, that ye do not rouse or wake my love, until he please.

fresh_translation: The voice of my beloved. Look, he comes, leaping on the mountains, springing on the hills.
brenton_translation: The voice of my kinsman! behold, he comes leaping over the mountains, bounding over the hills.

fresh_translation: My beloved is like a gazelle or a fawn of deer on the mountains of Bethel. Look, he stands behind our wall, peering through the windows, looking through the lattices.
brenton_translation: My kinsman is like a roe or a young hart on the mountains of Bæthel: behold, he is behind our wall, looking through the windows, peeping through the lattices.

fresh_translation: My beloved answers and says to me, "Rise, come, my dear one, my beautiful one, my dove."
brenton_translation: My kinsman answers, and says to me, Rise up, come, my companion, my fair one, my dove.

fresh_translation: Because look, the winter passed, the rain departed, went away for itself.
brenton_translation: For, behold, the winter is past, the rain is gone, it has departed.

fresh_translation: The flowers appeared in the land, the time of pruning arrived, the voice of a turtledove was heard in our land.
brenton_translation: The flowers are seen in the land; the time of pruning has arrived; the voice of the turtle-dove has been heard in our land.

fresh_translation: The fig tree brought forth its early figs; the vineyards in blossom gave scent. Rise, come, my dear one, my beautiful one, my dove.
brenton_translation: The fig-tree has put forth its young figs, the vines put forth the tender grape, they yield a smell: arise, come, my companion, my fair one, my dove; yea, come.

fresh_translation: And come, my dove, in the shelter of the rock, close to the forewall; show me your face and let me hear your voice, because your voice is sweet and your face is beautiful.
brenton_translation: Thou art my dove, in the shelter of the rock, near the wall: shew me thy face, and cause me to hear thy voice; for thy voice is sweet, and thy countenance is beautiful.

fresh_translation: Catch for us foxes, little foxes destroying vineyards, and our vineyards are blossoming.
brenton_translation: Take us the little foxes that spoil the vines: for our vines put forth tender grapes.

fresh_translation: My beloved is to me, and I am to him, the one shepherding among the lilies.
brenton_translation: My kinsman is mine, and I am his: he feeds his flock among the lilies.

fresh_translation: Until the day breathes and the shadows move, turn back; be like, my beloved, a gazelle or fawn of deer on the mountains of clefts.
brenton_translation: Until the day dawn, and the shadows depart, turn, my kinsman, be thou like to a roe or young hart on the mountains of the ravines.

fresh_translation: On my bed by nights I sought the one my soul loved; I sought him and did not find him; I called him and he did not answer me.
brenton_translation: By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loves: I sought him, but found him not; I called him, but he hearkened not to me.

fresh_translation: I will rise now and circle in the city, in the markets and in the squares, and seek the one my soul loved; I sought him and did not find him.
brenton_translation: I will rise now, and go about in the city, in the market-places, and in the streets, and I will seek him whom my soul loves: I sought him, but I found him not.

fresh_translation: Watchmen found me, those circling in the city: "Did you see the one my soul loved?"
brenton_translation: The watchmen who go their rounds in the city found me. I said, Have ye seen him whom my soul loves?

fresh_translation: Scarcely when I passed from them, until I found the one my soul loved. I seized him and will not let him go until I brought him into the house of my mother and into the chamber of the one who conceived me.
brenton_translation: It was as a little while after I parted from them, that I found him whom my soul loves: I held him, and did not let him go, until I brought him into my mother's house, and into the chamber of her that conceived me.

fresh_translation: I bound you by oath, daughters of Jerusalem, by the powers and by the strengths of the field, that you not rouse and awaken love until it wishes.
brenton_translation: I have charged you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the powers and by the virtues of the field, that ye rouse not nor awake my love, until he please.

fresh_translation: Who is this coming up from the wilderness like columns of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, from all powders of perfumer?
brenton_translation: Who is this that comes up from the wilderness as pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all powders of the perfumer?

fresh_translation: Look, Solomon's couch: sixty mighty men around it, from the mighty men of Israel.
brenton_translation: Behold Solomon's bed; sixty mighty men of the mighty ones of Israel are round about it.

fresh_translation: All holding a sword, trained in war, each man with his sword on his thigh because of terrors in the nights.
brenton_translation: They all hold a sword, being expert in war: every man has his sword upon his thigh because of fear by night.

fresh_translation: The king, Solomon, made for himself a litter from woods of Lebanon.
brenton_translation: King Solomon made himself a litter of woods of Lebanon.

fresh_translation: He made its pillars silver and its recliner gold, its seat purple, its inside paved with love from the daughters of Jerusalem.
brenton_translation: He made the pillars of it silver, the bottom of it gold, the covering of it scarlet, in the midst of it a pavement of love, for the daughters of Jerusalem.

fresh_translation: Come out and see King Solomon, with the crown with which his mother crowned him in the day of his wedding and in the day of gladness of his heart.
brenton_translation: Go forth, ye daughters of Sion, and behold king Solomon, with the crown wherewith his mother crowned him, in the day of his espousals, and in the day of the gladness of his heart.

fresh_translation: Look, you are beautiful, my dear one, look, you are beautiful; your eyes are doves behind your veil. Your hair is like herds of goats that were revealed from Gilead.
brenton_translation: Behold, thou art fair, my companion; behold, thou art fair; thine eyes are doves, beside thy veil: thy hair is as flocks of goats, that have appeared from Galaad.

fresh_translation: Your teeth are like a herd of shorn sheep that came up from the washing, all bearing twins, and no barren one is among them.
brenton_translation: Thy teeth are as flocks of shorn sheep, that have gone up from the washing; all of them bearing twins, and there is not a barren one among them.

fresh_translation: Your lips are like a scarlet cord, and your speech is beautiful; your cheek is like a piece of pomegranate behind your veil.
brenton_translation: Thy lips are as a thread of scarlet, and thy speech is comely: like the rind of a pomegranate is thy cheek without thy veil.

fresh_translation: Your neck is like the tower of David, built for ranks; a thousand shields hang upon it, all darts of the mighty men.
brenton_translation: Thy neck is as the tower of David, that was built for an armoury: a thousand shields hang upon it, and all darts of mighty men.

fresh_translation: Your two breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle, grazing among lilies.
brenton_translation: Thy two breasts are as two twin fawns, that feed among the lilies.

fresh_translation: Until the day breathes and the shadows move, I will go for myself to the mountain of myrrh and to the hill of frankincense.
brenton_translation: Until the day dawn, and the shadows depart, I will betake me to the mountain of myrrh, and to the hill of frankincense.

fresh_translation: You are wholly beautiful, my dear one, and no blemish is in you.
brenton_translation: Thou art all fair, my companion, and there is no spot in thee.

fresh_translation: Come from Lebanon, bride, come from Lebanon; you will come and pass from the summit of Faith, from the top of Senir and Hermon, from the dens of lions, from the mountains of leopards.
brenton_translation: Come from Libanus, my bride, come from Libanus: thou shalt come and pass from the top of Faith, from the top of Sanir and Hermon, from the lions' dens, from the mountains of the leopards.

fresh_translation: You heartened us, my sister bride, you heartened us with one of your eyes, with one chain of your neck.
brenton_translation: My sister, my spouse, thou hast ravished my heart; thou hast ravished my heart with one of thine eyes, with one chain of thy neck.

fresh_translation: How beautiful are your breasts, my sister bride; how beautiful are your breasts beyond wine, and the scent of your garments is above all spices.
brenton_translation: How beautiful are thy breasts, my sister, my spouse! how much more beautiful are thy breasts than wine, and the smell of thy garments than all spices!

fresh_translation: A honeycomb drips from your lips, bride; honey and milk are under your tongue, and the scent of your garments is like the scent of Lebanon.
brenton_translation: Thy lips drop honeycomb, my spouse: honey and milk are under thy tongue; and the smell of thy garments is as the smell of Libanus.

fresh_translation: A garden shut, my sister bride; a garden shut, a spring sealed.
brenton_translation: My sister, my spouse is a garden enclosed; a garden enclosed, a fountain sealed.

fresh_translation: Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates with the fruit of choice things, cypresses with nards.
brenton_translation: Thy shoots are a garden of pomegranates, with the fruit of choice berries; camphor, with spikenard:

fresh_translation: Nard and saffron, cane and cinnamon with all the woods of Lebanon, myrrh and aloes with all the first perfumes.
brenton_translation: spikenard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon; with all woods of Libanus, myrrh, aloes, with all chief spices:

fresh_translation: A spring of gardens, a well of living water and rushing from Lebanon.
brenton_translation: a fountain of a garden, and a well of water springing and gurgling from Libanus.

fresh_translation: Awake, north wind, and come, south wind. Blow through my garden, and let my spices flow. Let my beloved go down into his garden and eat the fruit of his choice fruits.
brenton_translation: Awake, O north wind; and come, O south; and blow through my garden, and let my spices flow out.

fresh_translation: I entered my garden, my sister bride; I gathered my myrrh with my spices; I ate my bread with my honey, I drank my wine with my milk. Eat, companions, and drink and be drunk, brothers.
brenton_translation: Let my kinsman come down into his garden, and eat the fruit of his choice berries. I am come into my garden, my sister, my spouse: I have gathered my myrrh with my spices; I have eaten my bread with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, O friends, and drink; yea, brethren, drink abundantly.
